article.intro: A snowman only lasts a few days, so it deserves a good name while it's here. This **snowman name generator** has snowy puns like Snowcrates and Brrrnard, grand titles like Lord Frostbottom, and cute names like Marshmallow, with a description of its look if you want one.

sections.heading: A short history of the snowman
sections.content:
People have been building snowmen for at least 600 years.

  • The oldest picture of a snowman is in the margin of a book of hours from around 1380, now in the Dutch national library in The Hague.
  • The Miracle of 1511: during a bitterly cold winter in Brussels, people filled the city with snowmen, many of them rude jokes about the politics of the day.
  • The usual look (coal for eyes and buttons, a carrot nose, twig arms) is just what was to hand in a garden or a coal shed.

sections.heading: Naming your snowman
sections.content:
The best snowman names are puns, and the worse the pun, the better.

  • Puns: Snowcrates, Brrrnard, Snowtorious.
  • Grand titles: Lord Frostbottom, for the snowman that took all afternoon.
  • Cute names: Marshmallow, Sprinkle, Twinkle, for the little ones.
  • Add a look to describe it on a card or a photo caption: "with a paper crown from a cracker".

For the reindeer to go with it, try the Reindeer Name Generator.

For the rest of the season, see all the Christmas name generators.

faqs.question: What's a funny name for a snowman?
faqs.answer: A snow pun: Snowcrates, Brrrnard, Snowtorious or Winterbottom. Choose the puns style.

faqs.question: When was the first snowman built?
faqs.answer: Nobody knows, but the oldest known picture of one is in a book of hours from around 1380.

faqs.question: What do you need to build a classic snowman?
faqs.answer: Wet, packable snow, coal or stones for eyes and buttons, a carrot for the nose, two twigs for arms, and a hat and scarf if you can spare them.
